study_title: The effects of psilocybin on psychological distress in cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
finding_summary: In two placebo-controlled studies, psilocybin was associated with higher Death Transcendence Scale scores than control.
support: In two placebo-controlled studies, psilocybin was associated with higher Death Transcendence Scale scores than control.
synthesis_interpretation: The result is reported as a significant positive effect.
meta_analysis_overall_study_count: Seven studies described as included in the review; placebo-controlled meta-analysis included two studies, and single-arm analyses included outcome-specific subsets of two to four studies.
meta_analysis_evidence_design_summary: Three double-blind controlled crossover trials, two non-randomized studies, and two long-term follow-ups of earlier studies are described. Most studies combined psilocybin with psychotherapy.
supporting_quote: the Death Transcendence Scale (DTS) demonstrated a significant positive effect (SMD = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.44 to 1.35, p < 0.001; I² = 0.00).
risk_of_bias_summary: Three RCTs had some concerns; two non-randomized studies received low quality scores. The quality assessment for the original Ross RCT was applied to its long-term follow-up studies.
extraction_warnings: The supplied text is internally inconsistent about study counts: the selection section says eight studies were included, while the study-characteristics section says seven studies. | The meta-analysis estimates should be interpreted cautiously because single-arm pre-post effects are not equivalent to controlled treatment effects.
